name: TX-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Ellzey's roughly 100-to-1 fundraising edge ($4.7M raised, $2.5M on hand vs. $44K for Minton)
R+11 district with a running incumbent
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 2%

model.rationale: Ellzey pairs an R+11 district and incumbent status with a towering money advantage, and prediction markets and the absence of any competitive signal all point the same way, supporting a double-digit Republican margin with minimal upset risk.
model.watch: Any polling placing Minton within single digits or a late surge of outside spending against Ellzey would be the first indication the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Rep. Jake Ellzey seeks re-election in Texas's 6th District, a seat whose partisan lean favors Republicans by about eleven points. Democrat Danny Minton enters the general election with a minimal campaign operation, having raised roughly $44,000, while Ellzey has raised more than $4.6 million and holds about $2.5 million in cash. No public polls track the race, and no expert ratings flag it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a two percent chance of an upset, and the district's fundamentals point the same direction. The expected outcome is a comfortable double-digit win for Ellzey; Minton's realistic path would require an unforeseen shift in the national environment or an influx of outside spending that has not appeared anywhere in the record so far.
